problem.title: Stronger Bell inequalities for Werner states?

question.summary: The source asked for a Bell inequality whose set of violating Werner states strictly contains the set violating CHSH. Vertesi constructed inequalities with many binary settings violated by two-qubit Werner states for p above 0.7056, below the CHSH threshold.
question.importance: Werner states can be entangled while admitting local hidden variable models, so they are the canonical testbed separating entanglement from Bell nonlocality; beating the CHSH threshold narrows the gap between known LHV models and the region of established nonlocality.

targetClauses.label: Bell inequality stronger than CHSH on Werner states
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks to find a Bell inequality whose set of violating Werner states strictly contains the set of Werner states violating CHSH, equivalently whose violation threshold is strictly below the CHSH threshold 1/sqrt(2) for two qubits.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: An explicit Bell inequality with a strictly lower Werner-state violation threshold, or a proof that CHSH is optimal on Werner states.

claims.title: Vertesi finds Bell inequalities beating CHSH on Werner states
claims.text: Vertesi constructs a family of Bell inequalities with many binary settings whose local bound and Werner-state quantum value give a violation threshold of p above 0.7056, strictly below the CHSH threshold 1/sqrt(2) which is approximately 0.7071. This is exactly the stronger-than-CHSH example requested by the archived statement.

evidence.sourceLocator: Many-setting inequality family with Werner threshold p > 0.7056
evidence.label: Physical Review A

decisions.rationale: The cited peer-reviewed construction exhibits a Bell inequality with a strictly lower Werner-state violation threshold than CHSH, which is what the archived statement requests.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: The Collins-Gisin I_3322 inequality cited in the source is inequivalent to CHSH but has a smaller Werner-state range, so it is not such an example; determining the optimal Werner-state nonlocality threshold is a separate question from the existence question settled here.
